attributes.board_name: Washington State Board of Physical Therapy (Department of Health)

rules.accepted_credit_types: No pre-approval; activities must relate to PT practice. Courses live/online (no limit), college courses (no limit; 1 quarter credit = 10 h, 1 trimester credit = 12 h, 1 semester credit = 15 h), science-based conferences (no limit), ABPTS board certification (no limit), electronic media without objectives (max 4), books/articles with written synopsis (max 8), presenting PT courses (max 16), peer-reviewed publication (max 10), clinical instruction of CAPTE/ABPTRFE students (max 10; 32 h mentoring = 1 h), certification courses e.g. public schools (max 15), passing the WA jurisprudence exam (1 h).
rules.new_licensee_rule: Must pass the Washington jurisprudence examination within the first full CE cycle after initial licensure (counts as 1 CE hour).
rules.audit_note: The board audits a percentage of licensees; audited licensees provide certificates/documentation per WAC 246-915-085 and proof of the 200 practice hours. Extensions only for emergencies.

topics.who: All PTs, every two years (WAC 246-12-800 to 830); counts toward the 32 hours
One-time suicide assessment training (screening and referral) from a provider on the DOH model list (WAC 246-915-086); counts toward CE
Pass the WA jurisprudence exam within the first full CE cycle after initial licensure

rules.notes: License renews every year on the birthday; CE is completed over two years. Also 200 hours applying PT knowledge (clinical practice or listed non-clinical activities) every two years. PTs with a spinal manipulation endorsement need 10 hours on spinal manipulation every two years (at least 5 on procedural techniques), counted within the 32. Current WAC 246-915-085 amended by WSR 25-09-054, effective 12/31/2025.
